ip_top_stories.title: Authors Sue Meta's AI Scientists Directly in Llama Copyright Case
ip_top_stories.summary: Authors have filed suit directly against Meta's AI scientists in connection with the Llama large language model copyright case, escalating legal action beyond the company itself. The move signals a new litigation strategy targeting individual researchers involved in AI training. This case is among the highest-profile copyright disputes involving generative AI model development.

ip_top_stories.title: UMG and Sony seek to add over 61k recordings to Suno lawsuit after discovery reveals AI trained on 'millions' of their copyrighted tracks
ip_top_stories.summary: Universal Music Group and Sony Music are seeking to dramatically expand their lawsuit against AI music generator Suno, adding over 61,000 recordings after discovery evidence indicated the AI was trained on millions of copyrighted tracks. The expansion significantly raises the stakes in one of the music industry's most consequential AI copyright cases. The move follows similar action by Sony against Udio.

ip_top_stories.title: MiniMax loses bid to dismiss Disney copyright lawsuit over AI system
ip_top_stories.summary: A US court has rejected Chinese AI company MiniMax's attempt to dismiss Disney's copyright lawsuit relating to its AI system. The ruling allows Disney's case to proceed and represents a significant development in copyright litigation against AI developers. The lawsuit is one of several major entertainment industry cases testing AI companies' liability for training on copyrighted content.

ip_top_stories.title: Sony Music Files to Expand Udio Suit, Alleges 30K Infringed Works
ip_top_stories.summary: Sony Music has filed to expand its copyright lawsuit against AI music generator Udio, alleging infringement across 30,000 works. The expansion compounds pressure on AI music platforms from major labels and parallels simultaneous action against Suno. Together, these cases could set defining precedents for AI training on commercially released music.

ip_top_stories.title: Artist Sues Copyright Office Over its Refusal to Register His AI-Enhanced Photo
ip_top_stories.summary: An artist has filed suit against the US Copyright Office after it refused to register a photograph he enhanced using AI tools, challenging the Office's position on human authorship and AI-assisted works. The case directly tests the boundaries of copyright eligibility for works that combine human creativity with AI generation. The outcome could have broad implications for creators using AI as a tool in their practice.

ip_further_links.title: OpenAI Must Produce Testimony From Musk Case in Copyright Suits
ip_further_links.summary: A court has ordered OpenAI to produce testimony from the Elon Musk litigation for use in separate copyright infringement suits, potentially widening the evidentiary scope of cases against the company.

ip_further_links.title: Can you own a voice? Taylor Swift's latest legal move raises big questions for AI and copyright
ip_further_links.summary: Taylor Swift's legal action over AI voice replication raises unresolved questions about whether a performer's voice can be protected under copyright or trademark law.

ip_further_links.title: Mind the Gap: States Step in to Address Ownership of AI-Generated Works Amid Federal Uncertainty
ip_further_links.summary: With federal copyright policy on AI-generated works unresolved, US states are beginning to introduce their own legislation to address questions of authorship and ownership.

ip_further_links.title: Japan eyes rules to regulate AI summaries' 'free riding' on news
ip_further_links.summary: Japan is considering regulatory measures to prevent AI services from summarising news content without compensation, as publishers push back against the practice.

ip_further_links.title: Europe's Copyright Trap Stalls AI Ambitions - Center for European Policy Analysis (CEPA)
ip_further_links.summary: CEPA argues that Europe's copyright framework is creating a significant obstacle to AI development, as unresolved licensing and training data disputes slow the continent's AI ambitions.

ip_further_links.title: Copyright and Artificial Intelligence: the divergence of the EU and UK
ip_further_links.summary: An analysis of how the EU and UK are diverging in their legal approaches to AI and copyright, with significant implications for businesses operating across both jurisdictions.

ip_further_links.title: Australian creatives urge the government to 'hold the line' on AI and copyright law
ip_further_links.summary: Australian creative industry groups are calling on the government to resist pressure to weaken copyright protections in response to AI industry lobbying.

ip_further_links.title: Media orgs push back against the relaxation of federal government's stance on AI, copyright
ip_further_links.summary: Media organisations are opposing moves by the US federal government to soften its position on AI and copyright, warning that creators' rights risk being undermined.

ip_further_links.title: Legal Risk Could Deflate the GenAI Bubble
ip_further_links.summary: An analysis argues that mounting copyright litigation and licensing uncertainty represent a systemic legal risk that could significantly constrain the generative AI industry's growth.

ip_further_links.title: The User Has Changed. Has Scholarly Publishing?
ip_further_links.summary: The Scholarly Kitchen examines how the rise of AI-driven research tools is transforming how scholars discover and interact with content, questioning whether academic publishers are adapting quickly enough.
